(a) Statutory Paygo Scorecards.—The budgetary effects of this division shall not be entered on either PAYGO scorecard maintained pursuant to section 4(d) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010. 
    (b) Senate Paygo Scorecards.—The budgetary effects of this division shall not be entered on any PAYGO scorecard maintained for purposes of section 4106 of H. Con. Res. 71 (115th Congress). 
    (c) Classification of Budgetary Effects.—Notwithstanding Rule 3 of the Budget Scorekeeping Guidelines set forth in the joint explanatory statement of the committee of conference accompanying Conference Report 105–217 and section 250(c)(8) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985, the budgetary effects of this division shall not be estimated—
        (1) for purposes of section 251 of such Act; and 
        (2) for purposes of paragraph (4)(C) of section 3 of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010 as being included in an appropriation Act.  
    (d) PAYGO Annual Report.—For the purposes of the annual report issued pursuant to section 5 of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010 (2 U.S.C. 934) after adjournment of the first session of the 116th Congress, and for determining whether a sequestration order is necessary under such section, the debit for the budget year on the 5-year scorecard, if any, and the 10-year scorecard, if any, shall be deducted from such scorecard in 2020 and added to such scorecard in 2021.

fable.w: This section only governs internal federal budget scorekeeping: PAYGO scorecards, classification of budgetary effects, and the timing of debits for sequestration purposes. The mention of an "annual report" might look procedural, but it is an internal federal budget report (OMB/Congress) and involves no outside party. There is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: The budgetary effects of this division shall not be entered on either PAYGO scorecard maintained pursuant to section 4(d) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010.

qwen_block.w: This section deals exclusively with internal congressional budgetary scoring rules and the maintenance of PAYGO scorecards. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations). The actors involved are Congress and its budgetary mechanisms, which are inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: The budgetary effects of this division shall not be entered on either PAYGO scorecard maintained pursuant to section 4(d) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010.

opus.w: This section only says how the division's budgetary effects are counted on PAYGO scorecards and in the annual sequestration report. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue. The references to conference reports, annual reports and sequestration orders are internal federal budget steps, so the participation test is not met.
opus.s: The budgetary effects of this division shall not be entered on either PAYGO scorecard maintained pursuant to section 4(d) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that references to a "PAYGO Annual Report," a "committee of conference," and a "sequestration order" make this look procedural. That fails because they are all budget scorekeeping steps inside the federal government (Congress, OMB and budget committees). No one outside the government takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section deals exclusively with internal federal budgetary accounting procedures, specifically regarding PAYGO scorecards and budget classifications. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any party outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private organizations). All actors and processes mentioned (scorecards, reports, sequestration orders) are internal to the federal government's budgetary management.
qwen_chat.s: The budgetary effects of this division shall not be entered on either PAYGO scorecard maintained pursuant to section 4(d) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section references "PAYGO scorecards" and "annual reports," it involves some form of procedural interaction or reporting that could be construed as participation. However, these are internal budgetary accounting mechanisms within the federal government (specifically involving the Office of Management and Budget and Congressional budget committees). There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with any outside party (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making a decision. The text strictly governs how budgetary effects are calculated and reported internally.
